claim: A no-tuning scikit-learn HistGradientBoostingRegressor with rolling mean/std/slope features (W=20) and RUL capped at 125 achieves last-cycle official test RMSE of about 14.2 (FD001), 16.1 (FD002), 13.7 (FD003), 17.9 (FD004) against capped truth, with NASA scores ~314/1247/382/1825, in 1.5-6 minutes per subset on a CPU laptop (script: baseline.py).
evidence: Direct reproduction, not just web research: I re-ran the cited script (C:/Users/HP/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-HP-OneDrive-Desktop-tata/f983720e-713e-4c7b-9ebb-a0f567283d43/scratchpad/scripts/baseline.py) on the locally downloaded NASA PCoE C-MAPSS files (scratchpad/dl_cmapss/.../inner/) with Python 3.12.1, scikit-learn 1.9.0, pandas 2.3.3, numpy 2.4.6 on a 12-logical-CPU Windows laptop. Data integrity: row counts match the official readme exactly (train/test rows FD001 20631/13096, FD002 53759/33991, FD003 24720/16596, FD004 61249/41214; RUL vectors 100/259/100/248), and the NASA PCoE repository page lists the dataset with the S3 download link. Re-run results (HGBR, last cycle of each test unit, capped truth, log at scratchpad/factcheck_run/rerun.log): FD001 RMSE 14.18, NASA 308.0, 133 s; FD002 RMSE 16.22, NASA 1233.8, 181 s; FD003 RMSE 14.08, NASA 457.8, 71 s; FD004 RMSE 17.88, NASA 1918.8, 203 s. Raw-truth (uncapped) RMSE: 15.42 / 27.90 / 15.71 / 28.92. RF (200 trees) capped RMSE: 14.36/16.94/15.31/18.16. Naive mean-RUL RMSE ~42-46. Comparison to claim: RMSE matches within 0.4 on all four subsets (FD003 14.08 vs claimed 13.7 is the largest gap); NASA scores match within about 5% on FD001/FD002/FD004 but FD003 came out 458 vs claimed 382 (+20%). Runtimes were 1.2-3.4 min, i.e. inside or just under the claimed 1.5-6 min band. Run-to-run differences are expected: the script uses early_stopping='auto', which the scikit-learn docs confirm is enabled when n_samples > 10,000 (true for all four train sets) with an internal validation split, and histogram-GB sums are thread-order dependent, so results vary slightly by machine/version. Caveat on "no-tuning": the script hand-sets max_iter=400 and learning_rate=0.05 (sklearn defaults are 100 and 0.1), so it is "no hyperparameter search" rather than pure defaults. Web search found no published RF/GBM baseline under this exact protocol to compare against; literature numbers (e.g. LightGBM+CatBoost ensemble RMSE 6.62 on FD001) are far better than this baseline, so the plan should present these as a floor, not a competitive result. The capped-vs-raw gap on FD002/FD004 (16-18 vs 28-29 RMSE) is material if judges ask for uncapped error.
correction: A scikit-learn HistGradientBoostingRegressor (max_iter=400, learning_rate=0.05, max_leaf_nodes=31, default auto early-stopping; no hyperparameter search) with rolling mean/std/slope features (W=20) and RUL capped at 125 reproduces last-cycle official-test RMSE (capped truth) of about 14.2 (FD001), 16.2 (FD002), 14.1 (FD003), 17.9 (FD004); NASA scores about 310 / 1230 / 460 / 1920 (FD003 and FD004 are noticeably worse than the claimed 382/1825 and vary by machine); runtime 1.2-3.5 min per subset on a 12-thread CPU laptop. Against raw (uncapped) truth the RMSEs are 15.4 / 27.9 / 15.7 / 28.9. Expect +/-0.5 RMSE and +/-20% NASA-score drift across machines and sklearn versions.
impact_on_candidate: Low. The baseline column reproduces: RMSEs are within rounding on three subsets and 0.4 off on FD003, and the script runs end-to-end on the official data in a few minutes, so the feasibility score stands. Two adjustments to the plan: (1) quote NASA scores as approximate ranges (esp. FD003 ~380-460, FD004 ~1800-1950) and fix the random seed/thread count or report a mean over runs, since judges who re-run will not hit the exact numbers; (2) state explicitly that the RMSEs are against RUL capped at 125 and show the raw-truth figures too (FD002/FD004 roughly 28-29), otherwise the model-performance claim can be challenged as lenient. Drop the phrase "no-tuning" in favor of "no hyperparameter search" because learning rate and iteration count are hand-set. The baseline is a floor, not a differentiator; published ensembles reach single-digit RMSE on FD001.
